strengths: Novel and reasonably well-motivated hierarchical Macro/Micro CoT decomposition for unified text-image reasoning, using masked attention to control which content is visible to which reasoning level, directly targeting a real practical bottleneck (token explosion in multimodal CoT with unified generation+understanding models).

The MDP formulation of the self-reflection loop (state/action/next-state/reward) is a clean and interpretable way to structure iterative image refinement, and is well matched to the training data construction pipeline described.

Strong empirical results relative to open-source unified models: improvements over the BAGEL backbone on GenEval and WISE, and state-of-the-art (among open-source models) results on KRIS, with competitive or superior performance to some closed-source baselines (e.g., surpassing Gemini 2.0 on KRIS overall score).

Practical efficiency claim is appealing and partially substantiated: the whole system is trained with only 8 A100 GPUs, which is attractive from a reproducibility/resource standpoint if the code/data are released as promised.

Good qualitative demonstrations (Figures 4-6) showing the self-reflection mechanism correcting semantically/physically implausible generations, and an interesting extension to 'Nano-Banana-like' compositional geographic image synthesis that illustrates generalization of the sequential decomposition strategy.
weaknesses: The paper is explicitly labeled 'Version 0.2' and openly defers core promised components to 'a future version,' most notably the entire Reinforcement Learning (DPO-based) stage described in Sec. 3.3 — no RL results, ablations, or reward model details are actually presented, despite RL being highlighted in the abstract/introduction as a key training ingredient for reasoning robustness.

Ablation studies are minimal: only an 'Uni-CoT Init' (no reasoning) vs. full 'Uni-CoT' comparison is shown in two tables (GenEval, WISE), which does not isolate the individual contributions of macro-level decomposition vs. micro-level self-reflection vs. the attention-masking design, nor quantify the claimed computational savings against a naive/flat CoT baseline.

Two of the three proposed Macro-Level planning strategies (Parallel Decomposition, Progressive Refinement) are introduced in the method section but are not implemented or evaluated at all in the experiments — only Sequential Decomposition and Self-Reflection are actually tested, making the methodological contribution appear broader than what is empirically supported.

No comparison to other CoT/RL-for-generation methods explicitly discussed in related work (e.g., T2I-R1, ComfyMind, image-generation-with-CoT approaches) that would be natural competitors; comparisons are limited to base image generation/editing models rather than reasoning-augmented ones.

The training data is heavily bootstrapped from proprietary models (GPT-4o for planning, evaluation, refinement instructions, and even 'ground-truth' edited images), raising concerns about distillation-driven performance gains, potential licensing issues, and limited reproducibility if this data/pipeline is not fully released.

Minor inconsistencies suggest the manuscript is not fully polished (e.g., Table 1 lists 'Uni-CoT' twice with different overall scores under the same name without clear explanation), and Sec. 4.2/4.3 headers are both titled 'Experimental Setup', indicating insufficient proofreading for what should be a finished submission.

The RL setup, when eventually included, is described only at a very high level (decoupled textual/visual DPO) without concrete details on reward model construction, preference data collection, or expected gains, making it hard to assess the soundness of a central claimed mechanism for 'training stability' and 'reasoning robustness'.

strengths: Tackles a well-motivated and practically important problem: the prohibitive token/complexity blow-up (~9,000+ visual tokens per step) when extending CoT to interleaved text-image reasoning in unified multimodal models.

The macro-micro hierarchical decomposition is conceptually clean and is backed by both a theoretical complexity analysis (O(T^2) -> O(T^2/M) -> O(T) via MDP-style micro transitions) and an empirical validation of token-interaction counts and training convergence (Fig. 4, Fig. 5), which is a nice combination of theory and measurement rather than only architectural claims.

Broad experimental coverage: GenEval, WISE for generation; MME/MMMU/MathVista/MMBench/Jigsaw-R1 for understanding; and appendix results on GEdit-Bench, RISE, and KRIS for editing, giving a reasonably comprehensive picture of the model's behavior across task types.

Useful ablations isolating macro-CoT vs micro-CoT contributions (showing they help differently depending on prompt/task nature), an ablation on the hierarchical training paradigm vs a naive long-chain baseline, and a base-model-swap ablation (BLIP3o) showing some generality of the framework beyond BAGEL.

The qualitative case studies (jigsaw puzzles, Picasso-style portrait editing, isohypse-to-landscape 'Nano-Banana-style' generation) are illustrative and provide intuitive support for the claimed reasoning coherence, and the isohypse-map experiment is a nice targeted test of compositional visual-transition reasoning.
Reasonably detailed reproducibility materials (attention mask diagrams, training hyperparameters, data curation pipeline, auxiliary loss definitions) and a stated code release.
weaknesses: Gains on general multimodal understanding benchmarks are marginal or even slightly negative relative to the base model (e.g., MMMU 52.7 vs. BAGEL's 52.8, MME-P identical, MMBench/MathVista +0.6/+0.2), suggesting the hierarchical CoT mainly benefits narrow reasoning-heavy benchmarks (WISE, Jigsaw-R1) rather than general VQA/understanding, which weakens the 'state-of-the-art performance and remarkable generalization' framing in the abstract.

On the RISE reasoning-informed editing benchmark, Uni-CoT (12.5 overall) remains far behind GPT-4o (28.9) and only modestly better than open-source baselines, so 'SOTA' claims should be scoped more carefully to open-source unified models rather than implying broad superiority.

The ~31K training dataset is small and heavily synthetic, constructed largely via GPT-4o/Qwen for prompt enhancement, subtask decomposition, and self-reflection supervision; this raises concerns about distillation-driven performance (i.e., partially learning to imitate GPT-4o's evaluative judgments) and about independent reproducibility given reliance on proprietary API calls for data generation, despite the reproducibility statement.

The parallel vs. sequential macro-decomposition strategies are introduced and shown qualitatively (Fig. 3) but not compared quantitatively against each other, leaving it unclear when/why one should be preferred or how the model decides which mode to use for a given task.

Complexity/efficiency comparisons are made primarily against a 'naive long-chain' internal baseline (Uni-CoT Raw) rather than against alternative efficient-attention or other reasoning-decomposition methods explicitly cited in the related work (sparsification, low-rank attention, hierarchical CoT variants), so the paper does not empirically position its efficiency gains relative to these alternatives.

Some notational inconsistencies/typos in the equations (e.g., z_i vs z1 in Eq. 3, s_{i,Ti} vs h_i^{Ti} in decoding, inconsistent sub/superscript usage across Sections 3.2–3.3) reduce clarity and could hinder precise reimplementation.

No human/user evaluation of reasoning trajectory coherence or interpretability claims (paper emphasizes 'coherent' multimodal reasoning but relies solely on automatic benchmark scores and cherry-picked qualitative examples), and no failure-case analysis discussing when the hierarchical decomposition or self-reflection mechanism breaks down.

The self-reflection/MDP-based refinement mechanism is conceptually similar to prior reward-model-guided refinement approaches (e.g., Guo et al. 2025b, Jiang et al. 2025) cited in related work; the paper could more clearly delineate what is technically novel in its self-reflection formulation beyond casting it as an MDP with a masking constraint.
